transcript:
MEETING HEADER:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 65 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mitchell (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Verdant), Priya Singh (Platform Eng, Verdant), Samir Patel (SRE, Verdant), Lina Gomez (Product, Verdant)

Summary (auto): Integration discovery for Verdant's chat + embeddings product. Focus on deployment modes, gateway/proxy placement, SDK/adapter compatibility, rate limits, and observability.

--- TRANSCRIPT ---
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood. With me are Maya and Diego, our SEs. How are you folks?
[00:06] Jordan (CTO): Good, thanks. Sorry for the slightly late start on our side, got pulled into an incident earlier.
[00:10] Priya (Platform): No worries. We've got about an hour, hopefully that's enough to cover the integration shape.
[00:15] Maya (SE): Totally, we'll aim for a 45-min technical sync then leave time for Qs and next steps. Quick agenda: hosted vs dedicated vs private, where you'd place a gateway/proxy, SDK support for LangChain/LlamaIndex, rate limiting/quotas, and what observability hooks we expose.
[00:30] Samir (SRE): Sounds good. Quick context: Verdant runs multi-tenant chat across EU + NA, we need PII guardrails, and our SLAs for user-side latency are 250ms tail for simple prompt responses. We currently proxy calls through our edge gateway.
[00:45] Diego (SE): Got it. Do you already use any third-party LLM providers or open models in prod?
[00:50] Jordan (CTO): We're piloting a mix: some hosted OpenAI for semantic search, and a couple of smaller open models in batch. The goal is to unify on a single inference path eventually.
[00:58] Alex (AE): Great. Two immediate questions — is data residency a hard constraint for EU? And is SSO + SAML required for admin access?
[01:05] Priya (Platform): Yes on EU residency for EU customers; we can keep dev workloads elsewhere but production must live in EU region. And yes, SSO is required.
[01:12] Maya (SE): Ok, good, that's aligned with Redwood Private/VPC options. Quick note on terminology — when I say "gateway" I mean the Verdant edge proxy that handles auth, routing, and rate limiting before the request hits the model endpoint.
[01:24] Jordan (CTO): Exactly. We want to avoid routing every token through our proxy if possible because of latency.
[01:29] Diego (SE): Totally understandable. We see two common patterns: 1) thin gateway that does auth/routing and forwards to Redwood hosted endpoints (fastest to market), or 2) sidecar/edge adapter that handles prefix cache locally and sends compact proto-requests to Redwood, which reduces per-token overhead at the cost of more infra.
[01:48] Samir (SRE): Can you explain the "prefix cache" approach? We have concerns about memory and KV cache coherence across nodes.
[01:55] Maya (SE): Sure. We do KV/prefix caching to avoid re-computing shared prompt context. In Dedicated or Private modes you can host the cache closer to your proxy to cut latency. On Hosted we provide managed KV cache — it's fast but adds a network hop. There's also continuous batching options.
[02:15] [Speaker 2 — inaudible]
[02:20] Jordan (CTO): How about the SDK story? We're heavy on LangChain and LlamaIndex in our pipelines.
[02:26] Maya (SE): We have official SDKs in Python/TS that plug into LangChain; also community adapters for LlamaIndex. We can send example code. For production we recommend our SDK with a small adapter layer in your gateway to handle retries, fallbacks, and tracing.
[02:41] Priya (Platform): Does the SDK do batching or should that be handled in our gateway?
[02:46] Diego (SE): Both options exist. The SDK can do client-side batching for micro-batching use cases, and our runtime does server-side continuous batching. For low-latency tails you might want client-side micro-batches + server-side optimizations.
[02:58] Jordan (CTO): We must know rate limit behavior. If we burst, do you queue or return 429s? We need predictable SLOs.
[03:05] Alex (AE): Hosted default is quota + rate limits with graceful queuing up to a brief window, otherwise 429s. With Dedicated you get dedicated capacity and configurable autoscaling policies and burst pools — so fewer 429s. For Private we can integrate with your autoscaler. We can share exact semantics in the SOW.
[03:23] Samir (SRE): Is there a per-account token quota or per-route? We have many internal services calling the same model so route separation is important.
[03:31] Maya (SE): We support per-route quotas and token-level tagging. In the console you can create per-route limits and set alerts. Also observability includes token-level cost breakdowns.
[03:42] [00:03:45 small crosstalk]
[03:48] Priya (Platform): Observability — we run Honeycomb + Prometheus. What's the easiest way to get traces and logs into our systems?
[03:55] Diego (SE): We emit OpenTelemetry spans and metrics; you can forward via our agent or scrape endpoints in Private. For Hosted we have a webhook and OTLP export option. We'll send example dashboards and a tracing snippet.
[04:07] Jordan (CTO): Security — KMS integration and audit logs. Is the KMS customer-managed on Private?
[04:14] Maya (SE): Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. Hosted supports envelope encryption with customer key up to an enterprise tier; Dedicated supports both. Audit logs (auth events, request metadata) are exportable to S3 or your SIEM.
[04:27] Priya (Platform): Nice. Any complexity with SSO provisioning and RBAC? We use groups and want coarse-grained RBAC for projects.
[04:35] Alex (AE): We support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and role-based access controls. We'll need your mapping but it's standard.
[04:45] [00:04:48 background noise - phone]
[04:50] Jordan (CTO): Performance targets — we said 250ms tail. Does Redwood have published numbers for hosted endpoints?
[04:56] Maya (SE): We publish median/95/99 latency for reference models. For typical Llama2-like models at 512 tokens, hosted median can be ~60-120ms depending on model, with 95th maybe 300ms for heavier models. Dedicated gives tighter SLOs. We'll propose a small benchmark pilot so we can replicate your traffic shape.
[05:18] Priya (Platform): That pilot — what does it look like? We want to validate both embeddings pipelines (bulk) and chat (low-latency).
[05:25] Diego (SE): For chat we'd run tail-latency tests with your prompt distributions and prefix lengths. For embeddings we'd run throughput tests. Pilot usually 2 weeks: week 1 install + connectivity + smoke tests, week 2 run benchmarks and review.
[05:36] Lina (Product): Will we need to change prompts or model format? We use some function-calling patterns and structured JSON outputs.
[05:43] Maya (SE): We support function/tool calling and can enforce structured output with schemas. The SDK has helpers to validate structure. Function calling does add complexity to batching but we handle it.
[05:55] Jordan (CTO): On the gateway architecture, we're debating two approaches: keep a thin auth-only gateway and have Redwood handle rest, or keep a richer gateway with local prefix caches. What's your recommendation?
[06:04] Diego (SE): If latency is the highest priority and you have strong infra, the richer gateway with local cache reduces round trips. If you want faster time-to-market and less operational burden, thin gateway + Redwood Dedicated is often the sweet spot.
[06:18] Samir (SRE): What's the maintenance burden of Private vs Dedicated? We prefer less ops but still need SAAS-compliant controls.
[06:25] Alex (AE): Dedicated is managed by Redwood and gives predictable throughput without you running infra. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives the most control but requires your infra team to operate/patch. There's also a hybrid where control plane is managed and data plane sits in your VPC.
[06:40] [00:06:45 speaker mislabel]
[06:46] Priya (Platform): Do you have a Helm chart or operator for the sidecar/gateway integration?
[06:51] Maya (SE): Yes, we can provide a Helm chart and a lightweight adapter (MIT licensed) that implements the LangChain/LlamaIndex hooks and sends compact protobuf payloads to reduce network overhead. We'll share that repo.
[07:05] Jordan (CTO): What about multi-region active-active? We have EU and NA users and want local routing.
[07:11] Diego (SE): We recommend regional Redwood clusters with smart routing. Our routing policy can route per region and fail over to other regions, with automatic fallback if capacity is constrained. There is also a cost-vs-latency knob.
[07:25] Samir (SRE): Billing — token charge granularity for shared endpoints vs per-customer? We need predictable unit economics to build pricing model for our customers.
[07:33] Alex (AE): We do per-token metering and provide per-route cost breakdowns. For Dedicated you can get flat capacity pricing + overage. For Hosted it's purely per-token plus optional retention/observability add-ons. We can model your expected spend as part of the SOW.
[07:48] [00:08:00 slight echo]
[07:53] Priya (Platform): One more on quotas: If one tenant spikes, can we isolate their usage so it doesn't impact others?
[07:59] Maya (SE): Yes. You can configure per-tenant quotas and circuit-breakers at the gateway level and enforce per-route throttles in Redwood. With Dedicated you can reserve burst pools by tenant allocations.
[08:12] Jordan (CTO): Any gotchas we should be aware of migrating from current OpenAI-hosted to Redwood?
[08:18] Diego (SE): Prompt formatting is generally the same but model semantics differ slightly; we'd advise running a small A/B test to validate output quality. Also, function calling schemas may need minor adaptation. We support evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[08:32] Lina (Product): Eval tooling — can we hook our existing test harness?
[08:36] Maya (SE): Yes, we have APIs for eval ingestion and can run quality monitoring. You can feed in prompt sets and get regression alerts if a rollout changes behavior.
[08:45] [00:08:50 crosstalk]
[08:52] Alex (AE): Ok, let's surface the immediate follow-ups. We will: share pricing + SOW, send SDK/adapter repo + Helm chart, and schedule pilot kickoff. Verdant to share traffic profile and target prompts.
[09:05] Jordan (CTO): Sounds good. A couple small clarifications — for Private, will we still get Redwood console observability or is that on-prem?
[09:12] Maya (SE): For Private there's an option: push metrics to your observability or stream to Redwood console (with enterprise networking). Most customers keep observability in-house for compliance, but we can integrate.
[09:25] Priya (Platform): Regarding KMS — do you support customer keys in Dedicated right away or is that enterprise-only?
[09:31] Alex (AE): Customer-managed keys are typically enterprise, but in Dedicated we can enable it as part of the contract. We'll mark that in the SOW.
[09:40] [00:09:45 brief pause]
[09:47] Samir (SRE): About rate-limits again — do you have a token-bucket implementation and can we set dynamic policies?
[09:53] Diego (SE): Yes, token-bucket style enforcement, and we expose policy APIs for dynamic updates. You can set per-route weights and change at runtime.
[10:03] Lina (Product): Who typically owns the SDK adapter maintenance? If we fork the adapter to add custom auth, do you maintain compatibility?
[10:10] Maya (SE): We maintain the upstream adapter; if you fork we can collaborate on patches but maintenance of your fork is on your side. We do try to keep adapters stable and provide breaking-change notices before major changes.
[10:22] Jordan (CTO): Ok, timeline — we'd like to start pilot by end of month if possible. Does that align?
[10:28] Alex (AE): Yes, we can do that. Action items: we'll send SOW and sample code this week. Can we get your traffic profile and a security contact to fill out the questionnaire?
[10:38] Priya (Platform): I'll own the traffic profile and coordinate the security questionnaire.
[10:41] [00:10:43 overlap: speaker unlabeled]
[10:45] Alex (AE): Perfect. Anything else from Verdant?
[10:48] Jordan (CTO): One last question — are there any restrictions on token masking or PII redaction built into runtime?
[10:54] Maya (SE): We have token-level redaction hooks and can run an in-flight PII filter in your gateway. For Hosted there are prebuilt libraries, for Private you can deploy custom filters. We'll share details.
[11:07] Priya (Platform): Great. That covers it. We'll look for the SOW and code samples.
[11:11] Alex (AE): Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after we share materials and align on pilot dates.
[11:16] Jordan (CTO): Thanks all.

END OF TRANSCRIPT

Notes: occasional transcription errors in names and acronyms; timestamps sampled roughly every 30-90 seconds. References to shared artifacts: Redwood repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-adapters (link to be shared by Maya), SOW template (internal link to be sent by Alex).
